label: Update campaign definition
description: Correct a campaign's definition — send only the fields you are changing. An omitted field keeps its value; an empty string, empty list or null clears it — except name, which a campaign always has, so clearing it is a 422. An unknown field name is rejected with 422 rather than silently ignored, so a typo can never look like a successful write. Returns the full definition as it now stands. Re-aiming costs leads. Changing target_role, target_geography, target_company_size, positive_criteria or negative_criteria is a retarget, exactly as in the app: the leads this campaign has not contacted yet are dropped and Explee searches again against the new targeting. Editing the offer or the email briefs does not — it only changes what is written to the leads still to come. Emails already sent are never affected. The rule for this endpoint: anything a person can edit on the campaign in the app, you can edit here — with the exceptions below, each of which exists because the app validates it in a second step this endpoint cannot reproduce. Read-only here: instructions and followup_instructions (the copy briefs — the app moderates them right after saving and shows you the verdict; this endpoint has no preview to show, and an unmoderated brief only fails later, at send time), target_url and reply_instructions (their own two-step save), keywords (Explee derives it; read-only in the app too) and followups (a project-level setting shared by every campaign of the project: sending the current values back is accepted, different ones are a 422). Budget has PATCH /public/api/v1/autogtm/campaigns/{campaign_id}/budget, status has start / stop. You can still SET the briefs when you create a campaign — POST /public/api/v1/autogtm/campaigns/import takes instructions, followup_instructions and language.

label: Create a campaign from your own leads (import)
description: Create a new campaign from your own lead list (async). Each call creates a new campaign in the given project — the campaign is built for your leads only (no agent lead discovery) and starts sending automatically once live, within your project budget. How it works: Submit project_id, a campaign name, and up to 30,000 leads Receive a task_id immediately Poll GET /public/api/v1/autogtm/campaigns/import/{task_id} until completed result.campaign_id is your new campaign — it appears in the campaigns list Per lead — mandatory: email, first_name, last_name, company_domain, job_title; recommended: linkedin_url (enriches the lead from Explee's contact base for a richer email). Leads missing mandatory fields are skipped (reported in the result), never a request-level error. Duplicates of leads already contacted in the project and do-not-contact entries are dropped. Your copy brief — optional instructions (first email), followup_instructions (all follow-ups) and language: the same brief you would type in the app's email editor, set here at import time so no manual step is needed. Omit them and the campaign is briefed from your project description alone. Pricing: the import itself is free. Emails are verified at send time at Explee's cost; sending is billed as usual.

label: Suppress people
description: Store a list of people to suppress — the same lists the Suppress list page in the app shows, so a list pushed from your CRM sits next to the CSVs your team uploaded and behaves identically. The suppress list is organization-wide: it applies to every AutoGTM campaign, running or not. Every email is checked against it right before it goes out, so an address added here stops a sequence that is already mid-flight, not just future ones. Matching is exact: a person by their email address (case-insensitive, but jane+crm@acme.com and jane@acme.com are two different entries), a company by its domain (the lead's company domain or the domain of its email address — acme.com does not cover eu.acme.com, list each domain you use). One call = one list, exactly like uploading one CSV: a list name that is already taken gets a (2) suffix rather than merging, and lists are independent — the same person on two lists is suppressed until both are gone. Delete a list you no longer want. Each person needs at least one identifier: an email, a LinkedIn URL, or a full name; a row left without a usable one (including a malformed address) comes back in skipped instead of failing the whole batch. Outreach stops on the email — the name and LinkedIn fields are stored but not actively used today; they are kept because a suppressed person is more than their email address, and the day outreach runs somewhere other than email (LinkedIn and the like) those are the fields that will match. To suppress everyone at a company use the companies endpoint.
